newsitem.title: USA: Goldman sees 25-bps U.S. rate hike on March 25.
newsitem.headline: Goldman sees 25-bps U.S. rate hike on March 25.

text.p: Goldman, Sachs and Co. said on Friday it expects the Federal Reserve to hike the 5.25-percent federal funds rate by 25 basis points when it convenes on March 25.

"Strong activity data, combined with a Fed chairman who believes that monetary policy tightening must be preemptive, suggests that Fed officials will decide to tighten monetary policy by 25 basis points at the March FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting," Goldman chief economist William Dudley forecast.

"Earlier, we had been undecided about whether they would move in March or wait until May. Our forecast of 125 basis points tightening over the next 12 to 18 months is unchanged... and well above the market consensus," Dudley added.
The Fed's last move was to lower the funds rate by 25 points on January 31, 1996.
The Fed last raised the funds rate on February 1, 1995, bringing it to 6.0 percent, a cycle high.
